data.title: Neon Gate Run
data.statement:
Midnight has fallen over Neon City.

A courier must escape the city by crossing [[N]] security gates in a fixed order.

Each gate follows its own repeating schedule. Some gates open frequently, while others remain closed for long periods.

You begin your escape at global minute {{0}}.

<<Your mission:>> Calculate the earliest global minute at which the courier can pass all [[N]] security gates.

<<Rules:>>

1. Travel [[T]] minutes to reach the next gate.
2. Each gate repeats its opening schedule every [[P]] minutes.
3. The gate remains open for [[W]] consecutive minutes per cycle, starting at phase offset [[O]].
4. If the gate is open when you arrive, you cross immediately.
5. If the gate is closed, you must wait until its next opening.
6. Crossing an open gate takes {{0}} minutes.

<<Gate opening condition:>>

A gate is open at global minute [[t]] exactly when:

(([[t]] - [[O]]) modulo [[P]]) < [[W]]

Here, modulo means the non-negative remainder between {{0}} and [[P]] - {{1}}.

<<Important:>>

All security gates use the same global clock.

Waiting at one gate does not reset or change the opening schedules of any other gates.

You must cross the gates in their given order. You cannot skip a gate or travel backward.

<<Example explanation:>>

The courier must cross {{4}} gates.

<<Gate 1:>>
Arrive at minute {{3}}. The gate is closed. Wait until minute {{5}}.

<<Gate 2:>>
Arrive at minute {{9}}. The gate is closed. Wait until minute {{13}}.

<<Gate 3:>>
Arrive at minute {{15}}. The gate is closed. Wait until minute {{19}}.

<<Gate 4:>>
Arrive at minute {{20}}. The gate is closed. Wait until minute {{23}}.

The earliest possible escape time is therefore {{23}} minutes.

2. Each gate repeats its opening schedule every P minutes.

5. If the gate is closed, you must wait until its next opening.

A gate is open at global minute t exactly when:

((t - O) modulo P) < W

Here, modulo means the non-negative remainder between 0 and P - 1.

Important:

All security gates use the same global clock.

Waiting at one gate does not reset or change the opening schedules of any other gates.

You must cross the gates in their given order. You cannot skip a gate or travel backward.

Example explanation:

The courier must cross 4 gates.

Gate 1:
Arrive at minute 3. The gate is closed. Wait until minute 5.

Gate 2:
Arrive at minute 9. The gate is closed. Wait until minute 13.

Gate 3:
Arrive at minute 15. The gate is closed. Wait until minute 19.

Gate 4:
Arrive at minute 20. The gate is closed. Wait until minute 23.

The earliest possible escape time is therefore 23 minutes.
Input
Line 1: An integer N, the number of security gates.

Next N lines: Four space-separated integers T, P, W, and O, describing each gate in the order they must be crossed.

T: Travel time in minutes to reach the gate from the previous gate (or the starting point).

P: Length of the gate's repeating cycle in minutes.

W: Number of consecutive minutes the gate stays open during each cycle.

O: Opening phase offset in minutes.
Output
Line 1: A single integer representing the earliest global minute at which the courier has passed all N security gates.
Constraints
1 <= N <= 100000

0 <= T <= 1000000000

1 <= P <= 1000000000

1 <= W <= P

0 <= O < P

All input values are integers.

The final answer may require a 64-bit integer.
Example
Input
4
3 5 2 0
4 6 2 1
2 7 3 5
1 4 1 3
Output
23
